rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: Hepatitis E is a liver infection caused by hepatitis E virus.

rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: The virus can infect both humans and animals.

rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: In the UK, foodborne exposure can include undercooked pork and pork products.

rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: Cooking meat thoroughly reduces foodborne hepatitis E risk.

rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: Handwashing after handling raw meat helps prevent cross-contamination.

rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: People with suppressed immune systems can develop persistent infection.

rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: Pregnancy and some underlying health conditions can increase the risk of severe disease.

rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: UKHSA guidance supports surveillance, diagnosis and health-protection response to reports of infection.

rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: Hepatitis-E risk depends on viral strain, food source, cooking, cross-contamination, immunity, pregnancy and clinical status.

rows.source: UKHSA and FSA hepatitis E prevention
rows.verified: Hepatitis-E evidence is food-, exposure-, person-, clinical- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: Cryptosporidium is a parasite that can contaminate water, food, animals and surfaces.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: Infection can follow contact with infected people or animals or swallowing contaminated water.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: Handwashing with soap and warm water is important after animal contact and toileting.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: People should not drink untreated water or swallow recreational water.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: Fruit and vegetables should be washed or peeled before eating.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: People with diarrhoea should stay away from work or school until symptom-free for at least 48 hours.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: Swimming should be avoided during illness and for 2 weeks after diarrhoea stops.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: UKHSA investigates outbreaks and works to identify and control the source.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: Cryptosporidium risk depends on water treatment, animal contact, hygiene, exposure dose, immunity, setting and outbreak controls.

rows.source: UKHSA cryptosporidiosis prevention
rows.verified: Cryptosporidium evidence is source-, water-, exposure-, person- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
